I don't know what version of mint you are on, but rafaela is on libreoffice 4.4.3. http://packages.linuxmint.com/search.php?keyword=libreoffice&release=any&section=any

I don't think mint is a rolling release distro, so you might have to wait a couple of days until 5 is in the mint repositories.

No you don't have to run both Update Manager and Synaptic. Both are just front-ends for apt-get, which you could (and in my opinion should) be running from the command line. (sudo apt-get update; sudo apt-get upgrade)

You're not seeing the newest version of LibreOffice because what's in the repos is the latest version that's been vetted for use with everything else. The assumption is that anything in the repos should be stable and not cause issues, so it takes a bit of time for the team to do the testing with the new version of any software and make sure there's no conflicts with the other things in that distro. Unless you need the latest version, it's much easier, and typically causes less headaches, to just trust what's in the repos and get the update when it comes.

If you want to always have the latest/greatest versions of software, then you should choose a distro that does that, like Arch.

To clarify what is being said, Mint is based on Ubuntu. Ubuntu does not update packages that jump a major version number mid release. This is because when a release is made, it is meant to be the same throughout it's lifetime. You should not wake up one day and find that an update hosed your PC or changed everything around on you. This is a good thing mostly, unless you want the latest and greatest of everything.

It will probably be included in the next new release of Mint/Ubuntu, but as others have said, you can add the PPA to get that freshness now.
